rules: One subject fills the frame, usually centred: a face, mascot, logo or product that is bigger than everything else.
Most thumbs have no or very little text, at most 5 words, and many have 0 words because the brand logo is the text.
The subject is made into a story by damage or menace: blood, bruises, scars, flames, handcuffs, glowing eyes, screaming mouths.
Founder and tycoon films use an extreme expression, usually anger or a scream, close to the camera and looking straight at the viewer.
Rags-to-riches films show a dirty child or a hoodie-wearing poor person against a luxury brand, so the contrast carries the story.
Money appears in many thumbs as stacks, piles or flying notes, and these are placed along the bottom edge in front of the subject.
Each film is built from its brand's own colours: Coke red, Pepsi blue, Gucci red and green, Netflix red; colours that clash with the brand are avoided.
Backgrounds are saturated, busy and symmetrical, often with logos, flames, flags, code or columns placed equally either side of the hero.
When text is used, it is large, high-contrast and sits in a bar at the top, over the subject, or in a blocky word along the bottom.
Brand names are written large in the brand's own style (script, serif, wordmark) and fill the frame instead of generic captions.
Fire is used on logos and backgrounds to signal collapse or scandal, and flames go on the sides or behind the logo.
A repeatable template (e.g. 'The DARK TRUTH of' above a glass of cola) is reused for parallel brand pairs.
